title: Computers in Singapore hospitals stop working

paragraphs: A nine-and-a-half-hour IT outage that disrupted Singapore’s public healthcare clusters on October 13 was caused by a preventable error by an IT contractor.

Senior Minister of State for Health told Parliament that the service provider failed to complete a required security update to the system. The disruption affected appointment bookings, medication dispensing, and billing across three major healthcare clusters. About 4,000 outpatient appointments had to be rescheduled. Although backup data centers were in place, both relied on the same shared system, which prevented an immediate recovery.

Health officials confirmed that the incident was not a cyberattack and no patient data was compromised or lost. Healthcare workers successfully switched to manual procedures and ensured no patient safety incidents occurred.

paragraphs: On October 13, Singapore’s public hospitals faced a nine-and-a-half-hour computer system failure. It happened because a tech company hired to update security rules didn’t do the work on time.

The outage affected major services, including booking appointments, giving out medicine, and paying bills. About 4,000 patient visits had to be moved to other days, but no patients were hurt. Health leaders said the problem was not a cyberattack, and no private medical data was stolen. Doctors and nurses quickly used paper rules and manual backups to keep taking care of patients. The health agency is now checking the contractor’s work and fixing the system so that future technical mistakes don’t cause problems again.

paragraphs: Hospital computers in Singapore stop working for almost ten hours on October 13. An IT company makes a mistake. They do not update the safety software on time.

This makes it hard for people to get medicine, pay bills, or book visits. About 4,000 people must change their doctor visits to another day. But officials say that nobody is hurt and personal data is safe too. Doctors and nurses work by hand on paper to keep helping sick people.
Leaders say sorry for the mistake. They are fixing the computers so this does not happen again.
